title: Sustainability
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Sustainability.

concepts.def: ISO 14040 (2006) standardises cradle-to-grave impact assessment; covers extraction, manufacture, transport, use, disposal.
William McDonough and Michael Braungart 2002 book; biological and technical nutrient cycles eliminate waste.
Total energy used to produce a material; aluminium ~155 MJ/kg, steel ~30 MJ/kg, glass ~15 MJ/kg, virgin polymers ~80 MJ/kg.
Reduce, refuse, reuse, repair, recycle, rethink; design strategy for circular economy adoption.
Pre 1999 single-score LCA method aggregating ecosystem quality, human health and resources damage; updated to ReCiPe 2008.
Directive 2009/125/EC sets minimum efficiency for energy-related products; banned filament bulbs in EU from 2012.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sustainability — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sustainability brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sustainability.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which ISO standard governs Life Cycle Assessment principles?
Whose 2002 Cradle to Cradle inspired circular design?

numericals.q: Approximately what embodied energy does aluminium have (MJ per kg)?

free_texts.q: Which 1999 single-score method scores ecosystem and health damage?
